answer: In an agent economy, proof of personhood ties each human to one signing key, and that key posts an escalating bond: the nth identity an operator registers costs n squared in locked capital. A quill that signs duplicate attestations gets slashed along with the whole voyage of wallets it backed, so faking a thousand agents demands a millionfold stake before any vote counts. Weight follows locked capital, not headcount, so padding the spiral of names buys no influence and every rejected clone forfeits its bond. The attacker pays superlinearly, while an honest agent parks a refundable deposit.
